key_insight: Fixed-order out-of-time-order correlators in broad classes of local random quantum circuits retain inverse-polynomial circuit-to-circuit fluctuations at system-scale depths, so they do not strongly concentrate away as the system grows.
engineering_relevance: This supports OTOC-based protocols as potentially verifiable observables for quantum advantage on near-term hardware, where direct sampling is hard to validate.
method: Proved fluctuation bounds for local random circuits in any fixed spatial dimension.
Analyzed 1D Haar-random brickwork circuits and showed many gates contribute to the fluctuations.
Derived a classical algorithm with the first rigorous improvement over brute-force simulation of 1D OTOCs.
evidence_signal: The paper is theoretical: it provides provable inverse-polynomial fluctuation results and a rigorous classical algorithmic improvement, rather than experimental data.
watch_item: The work does not establish full classical hardness of OTOC estimation, so practical quantum advantage still depends on additional complexity and noise considerations.
paper_title: Towards verifiable quantum advantage with random circuits: Observables that survive concentration
